text: Terrible Machine, Wouldn't Recommend.. I've had this washing machine for a little over a year. I wish I had researched it before buying. My machine broke and I needed on quick so I settled on this one. My biggest problem with this washer, like everyone else, is that the clothes do not come clean. If you get mud on your clothes, don't expect it to come off in this machine. My sheets actually look cleaner BEFORE I wash them. When washing sheets, it leaves this terrible sediment-like gunk embedded in the material. It twists the sheets up so bad during its cycle, that you almost need a linen press just to get the wrinkles out. Wrinkles don't come out of sheets in the matching dryer, and I've taken to having to iron them. My towels are left with this awful smell that seems like they were left in the wash too long, even if you immediately remove them. However, I've found that color-safe bleach helps keep the smell at bay. I didn't have this problem with our previous machine....it was a standard, normal top loader. I will say the the delicate cycle seems to do great, and if you don't have jeans mixed in, the normal cycle seems to work well too. It's also kinda cool that if the load gets unbalanced, the machine will balance itself. For those few good points, I give this 2 stars. I won't be purchasing a 'wave technology' machine again.

More Trouble Than It's Worth. I've had this dryer for a little over a year. I really wish I could take it back. The first few months, it worked great. Then, it started making this rapid clicking noise. A technician came out and ran a diagnostic that showed the thermostat control was faulty and caused the heat to kick on and off. A new control was installed and 2 months later, it did it again. The technician came back and ran another diagnostic only to show the same problem. A new control was ordered and installed. It's been 2 months since then, and yesterday, it started clicking again. Unfortunately, now that my warranty is expired, I'm stuck with this problem. On top of that, the dryer now makes this roaring noise that sounds like a bearing in the motor is starting to fail. Also, the lint screen is a horrible design. It allows some lint to travel past the screen, which can be a fire hazard. I wouldn't recommend the Cabrio Series to anyone. Both the washer and dryer are poorly designed and are in no way worth the price you pay for them. They have a nice appearance, but that's all I can say for them.

Never buying LG again!. After being a lifelong Whirlpool owner, I took a chance on LG for a new washer and dryer combo. What a mistake! The washer stopped working after 10 months and now LG customer service can't find an authorized service center near me after almost a week. (I live in a rural area approximately 1-2 hours from a major city despite what Amazon says is my actual location.) LG said I need to wait another 3-5 days while another department reviews my "case" to see if they can find a repair service near me. (Hint: try searching the Web -- there's one about two hours away but I guess LG can't figure that out.) I know what they need to do: refund my money or provide a brand new replacement WITH ANOTHER 12-month WARRANTY because I'm pretty darn sure it will break too. What a total rip-off and what a huge disappointment. I know I will need a new refrigerator within the year and I'm 100% sure that I WON'T be purchasing an LG!

Not what we expected in an HE unit. We have owned this unit for several years. Bought it new from a local dealer at a great price. Pros: uses very little water, spins out to nearly dry, price. Cons: detergent drawer can be cleaned if taken apart and soaked in bleach water, which must be done frequently because the alternative is hazmat level mold. The cavity that the drawer slides into can only be partially cleaned, and we've tried everything other than taking it outside and using a power washer, which we've seriously considered. The markings on the front of the unit indicating wash cycles, etc. have completely worn off--they should be able to handle a little window cleaner without dissolving. The detergent drawer face cracked and chipped off pieces of plastic over time, and not from severe use. Forget about soaking anything in this unit, as it uses the aforementioned very little water. In short, we hate this thing, so we got rid of it this week, replacing it with an efficient top-loader.
Looks and works great. Very pleased with the delivery and they were .... Looks and works great. Very pleased with the delivery and they were easy to set up.

Worst washing machine EVER. This is the most expensive and the worst washing machine we have ever owned. In short, it DOES NOT USE ENOUGH WATER! My old top loader would completely fill with with water when washing the clothes. This LG front loader tries (unsuccessfully) to wash twice the laundry in only 1 inch of water at the bottom of the drum. The machine does not fill with water it just sprays some water on the lump of clothes as it turns. Rinse?? Forget about it. This machine is incapable of properly rinsing the clothes. The laundry detergent just keeps building up until (in our case) we started to get allergic reactions to all the residue on our comforters. If you purchas this machine you will regret it. Hope this helps. :-)

Had this for 9 years.. 9 years ago my wife and I purchased this side-loading 3.7 cubic foot Whirlpool Duet Sport Washer. The first year we noticed it got our clothes really clean and they came out very dry. It produced a medium loud sound when spinning on high. However, it would give an error message if we put too many clothes, towels or bedding in and had to re-start. We moved after the first year and we were very careful not to damage it. Over the years this washer became unbalanced and many more cycles had to be re-started. The timing became inaccurate- 1 minute left meant that there was at least 20 minutes to go. This past year it became much louder and my dad and I took apart the outer shell to see if there was anything obviously wrong. We found that the brick weight on the top had crumbled. In the end we had to wash small loads and use “medium” spin which was still incredibly loud. The plastic seal finally dislodged from the drum and clothing was getting ruined. Another downfall of front-loaders is the mold and muck that that gets stuck on and in between the plastic between the door and the drum even though we ran “cleaning” cycles, wiped it out and left the door open between uses. Very disappointed. We replaced it with a top loading LG.
Dont move without shipping bolts!. If you move it, make sure you put the shipping bolts BACK in the rear panel, or you will blow the motor and the main board.
Dimensions. For anyone wondering about dimensions.

DON'T BUY SAMSUNG!!!! We bought this .... DON'T BUY SAMSUNG!!!! We bought this very expensive washer 3 years and 9 month ago. Had an extended warranty for 3 years. Spinning recently started to be very loud, something is off. We called a technician who said the drum has to be changed and that several Samsung washers are having the same type of problem. The deep water option is a sham. [[VIDEOID:691a6c42a696e229ac582bf7c2ba83ef]] 1. The deep water option is a sham which is why we bought it. The drum doesnt fill more than 50% deep with deep water on and water level set to max. Many clothes will stay above the water line the entire wash cycle as the water is not deep enough to pull them under. 2. Also, the only rinse option is cold water which is not always the best option. 3. And there is no way to manually advance the cycle from wash to rinse to spin dry. Once you start a cycle, you have to wait it out. Not happy and very disappointed in GE.

It has been a great washer but for the price of the parts with me doing the work it would be cheaper to put the towards a new washer and you can bet it will not be a Whirlpool. Worst machine ever. This is the absolutely worst washing machine I have ever owned. I bought it based on a website review. Foolish me. I also bought the extended warranty which is a big waste of money. After just over 2 years of use it is having continuous problems with draining and finishing the load. Sometimes it adds times. Sometimes the dial moves from "normal" to "wash machine" mid-load. Sometimes it just doesn't drain the water and stops without finishing the cycle. The first time I called to use the extended warranty I was told that there were no servicemen in my area and one would have to come from the city that is an hour and a half away. Since the extended warranty only covers parts and not labor the service call just for driving here was going to be $275. I called someone local instead that charged $75. Unfortunately shortly after it was fixed it is having the same problem again. I agree with all the other reviewers who have said DO NOT BUY! I will never buy Electrolux again. I hate this machine!

Faulty Machine Junk. Bought this brand new from Lowes apparently it has numerous fault codes wish I hadn’t disposed of older working double stack . Customer Service is useless , I’m returning in morning to Lowes

My wife loves the washer and dryer Samsung WV60M9900AV. Hubby does not.. My wife likes the functionality of both the washer and dryer. Very large capacity. She calls them her Ferrari's. So far, after 4 years, no problems with either the washer or the dryer. However, the washer and dryer doors are very low to the ground. I was compelled to build a 12" high platform to elevate the appliances to a usable height. One should keep in mind these machines are not your average size washer and dryer. Each is taller and wider than typical machines. The washing machine clocks in at 320LBs. I built the platform out of pressure treated 2x12" with 12" on center 2x8" joists. I used 3/4" plywood for the top of the platform and recessed the platform floor 1/2" below the sides so neither appliance could jump off. When we sell our condo, these girls are not moving with us.

Glad I Purchased The LG3997. I purchased the LG WM3997 a couple of months ago for our new home, which is space-limited, we liked not having to use 220, and didn't want to install a vent. When we first installed the machine, we only had cold water, as the house is still under construction, and the hot water was not yet installed. During that time, I did notice that many things were not dry, particularly in loads of mixed types of laundry (i.e. the jeans would be dry but the t-shirts were still quite damp). We tried putting the drain lower, into a bucket, rather than near the top of the washer, as suggested in other posts. That helped, but did not solve the problem. After connecting the hot water and leaving it turned on, even during cold-water washing, things are much more consistently dry, even while keeping the drain at the height of the washer. For some reason, the hot water seems to be required. I really like being able to wash & dry without having to go switch things from the washer to the dryer! I often use the Fresh Care feature, which tumbles the clothes occasionally if you don't catch them just after they dry cycle completes. I do use liquid fabric softener, rather than dryer sheets, because I am not stopping it between cycles. In my dry climate, I really need the fabric softener, which keeps the static out of my laundry. In the summer, I will often put most of the clothes outside on the line, and the washer does allow me to stop without drying. I'm keeping this at four stars, because I don't like the problem of lint around the rubber gasket at the front of the machine. After almost every load, I need to wipe it out with a wet paper towel. I've not yet found a solution to this problem. I have this machine installed in combination with the [[ASIN:B00AUWTYN2 O3 Pure Professional Eco Laundry Ozone Washer System - Newest Generation and the Most Powerful on the market]], which allows me to do all my washing with cold water and little or no detergent. The machine arrived on time in our remote location, and the shippers communicated appropriately to let us know when to expect it. Purchased from Home Care Company. The water supply lines were included with this washer.

Do not purchase unless you like washing itty bitty loads. Thank goodness I didn't pay any where near this price for this piece of junk. I've had just about every brand of washer over the years and this one is the absolute worst. I had a choice between this model and the other GE non-hydrowave and I unfortunately chose this one. I've had it for a year and basically wash everything on Super Level and, even then, you can't put in a large load. It took forever to come up with the right combination and detergent so that my black dress pants weren't streaked with white. It you use Oxyclean powder, be prepared to mix it in with a big stick. Forget washing a queen comforter. I've learned to work around the ridiculous water levels by double rinsing on some loads and always running on super level. The one reviewer summed it up perfectly that GE lowered water levels in a machine to meet government regulations without proper engineering and testing. Very disappointed. Over the years I've bought GE Profile kitchen appliances and was very happy with them. Now they just remind me what a crappy washer I'm stuck with. I've had it for over a year now and will never buy another GE washer again. And I own 1000 shares of GE stock on top of it. As soon as I can break even on the stock price, I'm unloading that too. The bigger the load, the less likely you are to have clean clothes. It will wash only the clothes in the middle. I have had to pause cycles to adjust my clothes so that they all get cleaned. This machine is a JOKE. Do not let anyone talk you into buying this product as you will be extremely disappointed. Also, your clothes come out extremely wrinkled and stretched out.

So now here I am...2013 and my washer is broke again....not because I have over used it! I am a single woman...with no children so my washer isn't over used. I called whirlpool and told them my washer stopped working after almost 4 years to get someone out to repair it. They called me back today to tell me that it would cost too much to have it repaired...so they are reimbursing me for the original purchase price. Their washing machines have given me problems...but I haven't gotten anything but excellent customer service from them so I am going to give them one more chance. Got a new washer on the way.

Mildew haven. We have to prop open the door after washing to help prevent a mildew smell. Even with propping the door open, this this washer builds up a mildew smell over time. Mold grows behind the rubber gasket, so you have to pull that back every once in a while, and wipe out sludgy black lint. There are products on the market to help clean mildewy front loading washing machines, but they don't get out that sludge. The whole reason to buy a front loader is convenience, and I personally think this is less convenient than pulling clothes out of a top loader after every wash. This is a problem with a lot of front loaders, but at least one other brand (Maytag) is including fans to help dry them. I also would like to point out that this model has Vibration Reduction Technology-- but I am not sure what is reduced, my washing machine vibrates LIKE CRAZY. (BTW, this washer comes with protective blocks screwed to the back of them that you have to take off. When I complained about the vibrations they said to make sure those were taken off. I said, they were, and they basically said that's all they knew to tell me.)

Bought the extended warranty through them.. that may be the key to buu them from somewhere you can getvlocal service and support....had a minor issue that they fixed for me and both the washer and dryer have been amazing...busy household with 4 young kids so it gets alot of wear and tear.. have had them about a year and a half now...i saw so many bad reviews on these I wanted to throw in a good one because I really think they are great machines!

Con: if your short like me (5 ft), better get a stool to step on cause this top loader is deep! I actually have two washers and dryers (and 6 kids, so they get a lot of use), and I just had to replace my upstairs set. I liked the Electroluxes enough that I just bought a second set of these, although the second set hasn't been delivered yet.
Will never buy another LG. Current LG front loader did not even last 4 years. Spin cycle is like an airplane taking off, drum is now shot.

love my bosch. I bought the washer and dryer. My first experience with Bosch laundry equipment was in France. I tossed in heavily used travel clothing for three people and stains that had long since been forgotten came out! The clothes were clearly cleaner. With my own machines I found that I had to using the settings more carefully to get what I wanted. The same is true for the dryer. Both the washer and dryer have longer cycles than US manufactured machines. Once you get used to that and do a little fine tuning, you'll experience truly clean clothing that will last longer. There was a comment about the sheets balling up in the dryer. They do. That's the only thing I have to address during the cycle. If you want your clothes washed fast - this equipment isn't for you. If you want your clothes to last and be truly clean, it is well worth adjusting to the European washing system.

Junk. Bought March 2018, warranty expired March 2019. June of 2019 the washer began stopping midcycle. Wouldn't complete a cycle. Samsung sent a repairman who charged more than 50% of purchase price. If you're looking for a disposable washer, this is for you!
Solid. Nice solid machine that works efficiently.

Awesome Washer. Maybe it's because the washer that came with my house looks like it's from the 60's, but I am completely amazed by how awesome of a job this washer does. Design [5/5] The design is very simple - can be considered minimalist. The washer offers a ton of options, but the simplistic design keeps you from feeling overwhelmed. The best part is that the washer is deep and can fit a ton of clothes, but the unit itself does not take up a ton of space. Performance [5/5] With a simple turn of a knob or a click of a button you have an arsenal of options at your fingertips to determine the best wash for your clothes. At first I was a little surprised by how long it takes to do a full load (roughly 50 to 60 minutes), but once you experience how amazing the rinse cycle is, then you start to understand, and appreciate why -- the clothes come out damn near dry which SIGNIFICANTLY cuts down on how long the clothes need to be in the dryer, which actually saves you more time in the long run. TIP: As other reviewers have noted, make sure you place your clothes in a donut shape around the center of the washer. Make sure that the middle is always visible. This will give you an amazing wash EVERY TIME. Overall [5/5] If you are looking for a great priced washer that will perform well beyond your expectation, then look no further!

It does NOT rinse clothing well.. My dark slacks always come out of the washer and then consequently the dryer with some type of residue on them. My old washer never did that. I have to hand rinse them after the wash before placing them in the dryer. I was shocked that a clothes washer would NOT have a fabric softener dispenser! It's difficult to know when the wash cycle ends because it depends upon the weight/size of the load. A fabric softener ball dispenser does not work as well as a built in dispenser. Whirlpool really went cheap on this washing machine. About every other time we use the washer it STOPS at the wash cycle (we've waited for over an hour for it to continue) and won't restart without starting over. Talk about a waste of water and electricity! ADDED COMMENT: I am considering buying a different washer even though I have had it less than one year!

Running well after 12 months. We bought this for our condo due to limited space which required a washer / dryer stack. I bought the pair via Lowes but am now going to purchase the same item via Amazon for our 2nd condo. We rent out our condos and they are both on the 2nd floor so it was important that the machines are efficient, reliable and quiet. We get all three of these qualities with the Samsung. My one complaint is the machine does make a bit of noise as its entering a high spin cycle. Once it reaches a certain RPM however it settles down. Apart from that though I couldn't be happier. Clothes get washed well and there is plenty of room for large loads. The dryer is also excellent.

You will repair this washer every 2-4 years. I bought this on Amazon around four years ago. I am repairing this machine for a second time for the same problem. It has a defective design on the central drum bearning. That's the part that allows the drum to fit in the motor/drive housing and spin. Over a two to three year period of running normally these bearings will go out and they will need to be replaced. You can buy a new bearning kit for around $80 and repair it yourself if you're VERY good at repairing things. You will need to: 1) Completely dismantle the machine. 2) Lift the drum assembly which is very heavy. You must use a pully or have other people help. You will likely get hurt if you try this without ample help or equipment. 3) Dismantle the drum assembly and remove the bearings. This requires a machine press or a hammer and pin and lots of patience. 4) Insert the new bearing with the same amount of equipment and patience. 5) Reassemble the entire machine (all of it... the gaskets, hoses, shock absorbers, wiring harnesses, control panel, etc.). Or, you can do 90% of the disassembly noted above and spend $300+ on an entirely new drum assembly. Or, you can spend even more than that to have a professional repair it or buy a new machine. I would advise against buying this machine. If you have this machine already and hear it sounding like an airplane taking off then chances are this problem is happening to you. If you have the persistence to fix this as I've mentioned above then I suggest you look online for a video on how to do this repair. I bought the service manual from Samsung (which is a horror story all by itself) but it didn't help as much as the videos online.

Lint can easily escape from the lint compartment -- and from the .... DO NOT BUY!!! --- MAJOR FIRE HAZARD!!! The Samsung DV448AEP dryer is a poorly designed machine. Lint can easily escape from the lint compartment -- and from the poorly designed dryer drum -- and onto the bottom portion of the dryer where the electrical components, the heating element, and the motor are located. With a 12-month or less buildup of escaped lint a fire can occur - as did in our case five times. Four of the five times we called a repair tech referred by our warranty. The repair techs explained the lint buildup was the cause of the fires -- but - what they did not explain was the lint build up was due to the poorly designed lint compartment. Shocking! They're in the business of being able to detect poor design. And not one repair tech said - Hey - major amounts of lint - like this - should not be located in this bottom area. It wasn't until our fifth fire - when we took the dryer apart ourselves that we discovered the design flaws. Any idiot can see where the lint is escaping. Why the machine was designed this way is beyond me. Why no one has contacted us about a recall -- or to tell us this machine is a fire hazard is beyond me. Why professional experienced repair techs did not know about this issue - or couldn't figure it out by looking at the machine is beyond me. Samsung should notify every consumer who has purchased this machine and offer a fix - or a newly redesigned dryer. You cannot tell me they don't know about this issue. Do not buy this machine. Or if you do. Don't go to sleep - or leave your house while it's operating - or you may wake up to - or come home to a burned down home. Good luck! We purchased this machine 10/18/2009 - with four fire repairs over the first six years - the last fire in the seventh year of ownership.

What a piece of junk.. I bought this dryer because I have had such good luck with our TV and refrigerator. This dryer is 13 months old, one month out of warranty, and it has gone belly up. It will cost me half of what I paid for it to have it repaired. I may just purchase a new dryer but it won't be a Samsung.
Five Stars. Even better than I expected!

Our dryer drum cracked recently - turns out this is a common problem. We called LG, they said they would replace the drum, but then suddenly refused to do so. Their customer service is really just a sham. They have people who answer the phone, but they must be instructed to never do anything to help anyone. Don't buy this!!!. I have had this for about a year. I use the product as instructed. It absolutely does a TERRIBLE job at cleaning clothes. We have had problems with grease stains showing up on clothes after being washed that were not there prior to being put in the washer. It is crazy. About half of the beads were still in the washer!!! Do NOT get this. I will always check Amazon's reveiws first instead of looking at Lowe's. I find it out that the ratings are so different on the same model between the two sites...

They really need to do something about the agitator on .... They really need to do something about the agitator on this washing machine. Also, how did it get HE certification? This uses as much water as my old washer.

Horrible.. I purchased this machine May 24th. Yesterday, June 9th, I tried to use this machine for only the second time since it arrived. After the water went in, nothing happened. For several minutes the machine sat not moving, then an error code, ERR7, started flashing on the display. In the manual this code implies a problem with the motor, and upon research it seems that motors going out on Haier machines is quite a common problem. AGREED! The worst washer ever.. We bought this for our Mom who is in her 80's, so simple and efficient operation was important. It was advertised as being quiet, and the spin cycle is amazingly unobtrusive, but it screeches during another part the cycle, which alarmed Mom at first because it sounded like it was having mechanical difficulty (i.e. not the sound of a smoothly operating appliance). Having to go out and buy a special type of detergent was also a thumbs-down (although I understand the reasoning behind it). People may have their distinct favorite brand after several decades of doing laundry, or they may want to use coupons or buy detergent on sale if on a limited income and not be obligated to a higher priced item. One day I came over to did the laundry for Mom. I am fascinated with new technology so I peeked inside the tub mid-cycle trying to see how the odd-looking agitator worked. I was surprised to see barely any water in the tub, and the clothes on top were out of the water. I thought maybe I had forgotten to change the Load Size setting from small to large when I put in the load. Guess what? No setting for load size--it automatically fills so you can't add more water even if you wanted to. Then I noticed actually printed on the machine "It is normal for some of the load to be above the water level". Hello. Last time I checked, you actually have to have clothes IN the water for them to get WASHED and eventually, clean. The machine is advertised as high-volume capacity but what good is that when you can't fill the water up to that capacity? The concept is that the agitator will eventually rotate the clothes on top down into the water, and push the others out of the water. So, I get it, you use only half the amount of water necessary by making the clothes take turns getting in and out of their bath. But....are you really getting the clothes clean swishing them around in half the water, which is twice as dirty? And the clothes are getting washed only half the time that you think they are, because half the time they are waiting their turn to get rotated in? At the end of the cycle, there was just a little bit of detergent residue (using the high efficiency detergent) but the clothes still had dog hair on them. I had to redo the load which of course, negated the energy star effects for both water and electricity. Maybe if you never check the laundry afterward and just throw it into the dryer, you'll land up with more lint because the extra stuff got blown out instead of washed out. I understand you might not get everything out if you have tons of dog hair in there but it's not like she owns a kennel or anything, she has one little 15 pound dog. I have 3 dogs and my Kenmore (that actually uses enough water to wash the load) gets everything fabulously clean. So I think this is an example of a company being so excited about their new technology that they put it into production right away so they could be the first on the market, but actually thought it was not important to test it thoroughly first. What were they thinking? Truthfully, I wouldn't even get this machine it it were at the Goodwill.
